entities.name: Antiochus IV of Commagene
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antiochus IV of Commagene was a prominent client king of the Roman Empire, reigning from 38 to 72 CE. He was the last ruler of the Commagene Kingdom, a Hellenistic state in ancient Anatolia (modern-day Turkey).

    Born into a royal family, Antiochus IV's early life and reign were marked by power struggles with his Roman overlords and his own family members. He rose to prominence through his military campaigns, expanding Commagene's borders and securing its position as a Roman client state.

    The epithet 'Epiphanes' (meaning 'the Glorious') was bestowed upon Antiochus IV due to his military victories, particularly against the Parthian Empire. He also promoted the Cult of Attis, a syncretic cult blending elements of Greek and Roman deities, which became a distinctive feature of Commagene's religious landscape.

    Antiochus IV's reign was cut short by his death in 100 CE, marking the end of the Commagene Kingdom and its unique cultural heritage.

    In the centuries following his death, the legacy of Antiochus IV was largely overshadowed by the rise of Christianity and the decline of the Roman Empire. Nevertheless, his impact on the development of Hellenistic and Roman culture remains a topic of scholarly interest and debate.
